While studying abroad in Lyon in summer 2025 as a Gilman Scholar, I recorded bicycle rides with a GoPro and used the footage's GPS data to reconstruct the routes and turn them into an interactive map.

This grew out of my Gilman Scholarship follow on service project, which was designed to document Lyon's cycling infrastructure and make the city easier for future students to explore.

## How I made it

The basic workflow was:

1. Record rides around Lyon with a GoPro.
2. Extract the GPS coordinates associated with the footage.
3. Organize the location data into usable routes.
4. Load the routes into Google My Maps to create an interactive view of where I had ridden.

## Why I like this project

This started as part of my Gilman Scholarship follow on project and became an early experiment in working with location data I collected myself. Instead of starting with a downloaded dataset, I recorded the rides, extracted the GPS coordinates, organized the routes, and turned them into something other people could explore.

It was a simple workflow, but it was one of the first times I connected something I was doing in the real world with a data project.

:::
